001.text: ‘Tis time o’ the cunning, and thou art swollen wi’ it. There's power here, in the land, in the forests - but Nature shalbe not mocked - to wield her weapons ye must pay her a toll. What toll? Why nought but th’toll o’blood. Drag them to the table, let them hang, see their flesh burn in th’shapes o’wicker - from their bones new life shall grow; thy belly shall grow wi’ it. Ah, what sights ye’ll birth, O Cunning Woman. Send the Oss and drag them home, feed the land and go garlanded, love, for all shall bless thy dominion on the earth.
001.shown: ‘Tis time o’ the cunning, and thou art swollen wi’ it. There's power here, in the land, in the forests - but Nature shalbe not mocked - to wield her weapons ye must pay her a toll. What toll? Why nought but th’toll o’blood. Drag them to the table, let them hang, see their flesh burn in th’shapes o’wicker - from their bones new life shall grow; thy belly shall grow wi’ it. Ah, what sights ye’ll birth, O Cunning Woman. Send the Oss and drag them home, feed the land and go garlanded, love, for all shall bless thy dominion on the earth.

002.text: Watch the villages fight among themselves
002.shown: Watch the villages fight among themselves

003.text: Your village is ochre. {land}% land, {settings.enemies} rival(s). Pale marks are the Moot and the hollow hills.
003.shown: Your village is ochre. {number}% land, {number} rival(s). Pale marks are the Moot and the hollow hills.

004.text: Tap your people to select them. Tap the ground to move them, or an enemy to attack.
004.shown: Tap your people to select them. Tap the ground to move them, or an enemy to attack.

005.text: Drag with one finger to pan. Pinch to zoom, and twist two fingers to turn the world.
005.shown: Drag with one finger to pan. Pinch to zoom, and twist two fingers to turn the world.

006.text: Turn on Box, then drag to select a group. Double-tap a unit to select all of that kind nearby.
006.shown: Turn on Box, then drag to select a group. Double-tap a unit to select all of that kind nearby.

007.text: To clear your selection, tap with two fingers at once, press and hold on empty ground, or tap the selection line above the tabs.
007.shown: To clear your selection, tap with two fingers at once, press and hold on empty ground, or tap the selection line above the tabs.

008.text: Left-click selects your people, or tells the selected ones what to do; drag to box-select. Right-click on empty ground clears the selection; right-click on something still commands.
008.shown: Left-click selects your people, or tells the selected ones what to do; drag to box-select. Right-click on empty ground clears the selection; right-click on something still commands.

009.text: Right-drag turns the view, middle-drag or WASD pans, the wheel zooms. Space finds your Cunning Woman, keys 1–0 pick spells, F toggles full screen, Esc cancels.
009.shown: Right-drag turns the view, middle-drag or WASD pans, the wheel zooms. Space finds your Cunning Woman, keys 1–0 pick spells, F toggles full screen, Esc cancels.

010.text: Villagers chop wood, build, and go into huts to breed. From the men, a grave; and from the grace, a seed; and from that seed: the trees!
010.shown: Villagers chop wood, build, and go into huts to breed. From the men, a grave; and from the grace, a seed; and from that seed: the trees!

011.text: The forest altar takes one offering at a time and is stronger the more trees stand around it. The wicker man takes five and burns, giving mana and a frenzy of speed. The Wicker God takes twelve and burns for an enormous offering, terrifying any enemy who sees it. Both wicker figures burn down on use and must be rebuilt.
011.shown: The forest altar takes one offering at a time and is stronger the more trees stand around it. The wicker man takes five and burns, giving mana and a frenzy of speed. The Wicker God takes twelve and burns for an enormous offering, terrifying any enemy who sees it. Both wicker figures burn down on use and must be rebuilt.

012.text: Burning your own people fills the dread meter. Past the mark, frightened villagers start slipping away into the wilds. Dread fades with time, and faster with more huts.
012.shown: Burning your own people fills the dread meter. Past the mark, frightened villagers start slipping away into the wilds. Dread fades with time, and faster with more huts.

013.text: Osses, from the Oss House, roam the ground around where you last sent them and seize anyone they can catch, wildmen or enemy, carrying them home to your thrall fold at a run. Once an Oss has a captive it will not take orders until it is home. Captives are worth far more than your own people and cause no dread; kill an Oss on its way home and its captive goes free. You start with one thrall fold, which holds fifteen. Two or more captives left together in a fold will breed, slowly at first and then faster, so a fold left alone fills itself.
013.shown: Osses, from the Oss House, roam the ground around where you last sent them and seize anyone they can catch, wildmen or enemy, carrying them home to your thrall fold at a run. Once an Oss has a captive it will not take orders until it is home. Captives are worth far more than your own people and cause no dread; kill an Oss on its way home and its captive goes free. You start with one thrall fold, which holds fifteen. Two or more captives left together in a fold will breed, slowly at first and then faster, so a fold left alone fills itself.

014.text: Herne's Oak is a vast dead tree raised in deep woodland. Hang your Cunning Woman from it for two minutes, during which she can do nothing, and the Wild Hunt rides for you: antlered horsemen who roam the whole world killing anyone they find outside the reach of an enemy Cunning Woman. Every death they cause feeds you as richly as a captive, and lost riders return.
014.shown: Herne's Oak is a vast dead tree raised in deep woodland. Hang your Cunning Woman from it for two minutes, during which she can do nothing, and the Wild Hunt rides for you: antlered horsemen who roam the whole world killing anyone they find outside the reach of an enemy Cunning Woman. Every death they cause feeds you as richly as a captive, and lost riders return.

015.text: Build a Maypole and idle villagers will dance around it, easing your people's dread. After enough merriment a May Queen is crowned. The longer she lives, the more her offering is worth, up to a vast sum with no dread and a long frenzy. Select fighters and tap her to swear them as her guards; you can do the same for your Cunning Woman. Rival Osses will hunt her, and a captured Queen can be offered by her captors for her full worth.
015.shown: Build a Maypole and idle villagers will dance around it, easing your people's dread. After enough merriment a May Queen is crowned. The longer she lives, the more her offering is worth, up to a vast sum with no dread and a long frenzy. Select fighters and tap her to swear them as her guards; you can do the same for your Cunning Woman. Rival Osses will hunt her, and a captured Queen can be offered by her captors for her full worth.

016.text: Blackthorn hedges are cheap thorny barriers. Choose the hedge, tap where it starts and where it ends, and villagers plant it a length at a time. Nothing walks through a finished hedge, your own people included, so leave gaps; enemies must go round or hack through, which turns open ground into chokepoints.
016.shown: Blackthorn hedges are cheap thorny barriers. Choose the hedge, tap where it starts and where it ends, and villagers plant it a length at a time. Nothing walks through a finished hedge, your own people included, so leave gaps; enemies must go round or hack through, which turns open ground into chokepoints.

017.text: Your Bog is a hidden trap: your own people cross it safely, but enemies cannot see it and march straight in. It lasts until it has drowned ten of them. Fighters near their own buildings also take slightly less damage.
017.shown: Your Bog is a hidden trap: your own people cross it safely, but enemies cannot see it and march straight in. It lasts until it has drowned ten of them. Fighters near their own buildings also take slightly less damage.

018.text: When a rival army sets out for you, a horn sounds and the marching column shows on your map through the fog. An attack that loses half its strength breaks and runs home.
018.shown: When a rival army sets out for you, a horn sounds and the marching column shows on your map through the fog. An attack that loses half its strength breaks and runs home.

019.text: The Rook Tree is a lookout in a dead tree. It sees a long way and hurls fire-pots at any enemy balloon in range, bringing one down in three hits. It ignores everything on the ground.
019.shown: The Rook Tree is a lookout in a dead tree. It sees a long way and hurls fire-pots at any enemy balloon in range, bringing one down in three hits. It ignores everything on the ground.

020.text: To hold ground, select warriors or archers (the +5 buttons on the Tribe tab add the five nearest of a kind) and press Post on the selection line, then tap a spot. They form up round a banner, fight whatever comes near without chasing far, and take less harm while they stand at their post. Sending fighters to your oak, your tomb or a hollow hill posts them there the same way. Guards are left out when you select your army; give them any other order to take them off their post.
020.shown: To hold ground, select warriors or archers (the +5 buttons on the Tribe tab add the five nearest of a kind) and press Post on the selection line, then tap a spot. They form up round a banner, fight whatever comes near without chasing far, and take less harm while they stand at their post. Sending fighters to your oak, your tomb or a hollow hill posts them there the same way. Guards are left out when you select your army; give them any other order to take them off their post.

021.text: A tribe that loses every building, trained unit and its Cunning Woman is finished: its last villagers are dragged off as captives by whoever broke it. A tribe whose people are all dead hands its empty buildings to the conqueror, with an offering of mana.
021.shown: A tribe that loses every building, trained unit and its Cunning Woman is finished: its last villagers are dragged off as captives by whoever broke it. A tribe whose people are all dead hands its empty buildings to the conqueror, with an offering of mana.

022.text: Ground where a building has been razed is salted earth: for three minutes its old owner cannot build there. A rival that falls to a fifth of its greatest size is broken. Its people gather at their stone circle where everyone can see them, its buildings fall to disrepair and its Cunning Woman does not return; destroy her last fighters and the rest are yours for your pyres.
022.shown: Ground where a building has been razed is salted earth: for three minutes its old owner cannot build there. A rival that falls to a fifth of its greatest size is broken. Its people gather at their stone circle where everyone can see them, its buildings fall to disrepair and its Cunning Woman does not return; destroy her last fighters and the rest are yours for your pyres.

023.text: Tap a rival's marker at the top of the screen to look at where her people are. Tap again to move on to the next group.
023.shown: Tap a rival's marker at the top of the screen to look at where her people are. Tap again to move on to the next group.

024.text: Training buildings turn a villager into a warrior, archer, Oss or balloonist.
024.shown: Training buildings turn a villager into a warrior, archer, Oss or balloonist.

025.text: To cross water, have your Cunning Woman raise a Land Bridge from the shore towards the land you want. Anyone can walk it, your enemies included. Or, if you have balloons, simply order your people across: idle balloons fly to them, carry them over and come back until everyone is across.
025.shown: To cross water, have your Cunning Woman raise a Land Bridge from the shore towards the land you want. Anyone can walk it, your enemies included. Or, if you have balloons, simply order your people across: idle balloons fly to them, carry them over and come back until everyone is across.

026.text: Balloonists drift above the fighting and drop charges. Only other balloonists can reach them.
026.shown: Balloonists drift above the fighting and drop charges. Only other balloonists can reach them.

027.text: Wildmen wander the wilds. They make easy captives.
027.shown: Wildmen wander the wilds. They make easy captives.

028.text: Hollow hills are ancient barrows that await discovery in wild country. Send your Cunning Woman with twenty sacrifices and at least 1,500 mana to perform the ritual of attaining and seal her inside. The hill becomes a wicker fortress: from it she sees everything and casts anywhere at half the mana. If enemies tear it down she is lost for a minute, then rises at your stone circle, and half your mana goes with her.
028.shown: Hollow hills are ancient barrows that await discovery in wild country. Send your Cunning Woman with twenty sacrifices and at least 1,500 mana to perform the ritual of attaining and seal her inside. The hill becomes a wicker fortress: from it she sees everything and casts anywhere at half the mana. If enemies tear it down she is lost for a minute, then rises at your stone circle, and half your mana goes with her.

029.text: All-against-all needs an unlit wicker man, ten followers to burn and a full bar of mana. All shall leave their dwellings where they stand and make way to the Moot at the world's end, there to fight to the death.
029.shown: All-against-all needs an unlit wicker man, ten followers to burn and a full bar of mana. All shall leave their dwellings where they stand and make way to the Moot at the world's end, there to fight to the death.

030.text: Pick a spell and tap a target. Your Cunning Woman walks into range and casts. If she dies she returns at your stone circle after forty-five seconds while your tribe survives.
030.shown: Pick a spell and tap a target. Your Cunning Woman walks into range and casts. If she dies she returns at your stone circle after forty-five seconds while your tribe survives.

031.text: The Scrying Torch spell conjures a burning beacon where the Cunning Woman aims it. The land around it stays in sight for as long as it stands, which makes it a lookout over a pass, a rival's door or a hollow hill. Enemies can tear it down.
031.shown: The Scrying Torch spell conjures a burning beacon where the Cunning Woman aims it. The land around it stays in sight for as long as it stands, which makes it a lookout over a pass, a rival's door or a hollow hill. Enemies can tear it down.

032.text: Ättestupa: when fewer than three villagers are left, your Cunning Woman can raise a crag at the edge of the village, climb it while your people watch, and go over the edge. Six villagers step out of the stone circle, no rival attacks you for thirty seconds, and she is reborn as usual. The crag stays, and she climbs the same one if it ever comes to that again.
032.shown: Ättestupa: when fewer than three villagers are left, your Cunning Woman can raise a crag at the edge of the village, climb it while your people watch, and go over the edge. Six villagers step out of the stone circle, no rival attacks you for thirty seconds, and she is reborn as usual. The crag stays, and she climbs the same one if it ever comes to that again.

033.text: You win when every rival tribe has no followers or buildings left.
033.shown: You win when every rival tribe has no followers or buildings left.

035.text: Across the water a people keeps its own fires and will not answer when we call. Our Cunning Woman has no power of her own: everything she does must be paid for with a life. Build a forest altar among the trees and give it villagers, one at a time. With what it gives back, raise warriors, lift the sea floor into a road, and cross.
035.shown: Across the water a people keeps its own fires and will not answer when we call. Our Cunning Woman has no power of her own: everything she does must be paid for with a life. Build a forest altar among the trees and give it villagers, one at a time. With what it gives back, raise warriors, lift the sea floor into a road, and cross.

037.text: The grove gives a little for each life. The wicker man gives far more, but it takes five at once, and it must burn to give anything at all. Feed it, and the Cunning Woman will have what she needs.
037.shown: The grove gives a little for each life. The wicker man gives far more, but it takes five at once, and it must burn to give anything at all. Feed it, and the Cunning Woman will have what she needs.

039.text: The wild folk wander the woods with no hearth and no name. The Oss will bring them in. Fill the fold with ten of them and the people will know we can feed the fires for a long winter.
039.shown: The wild folk wander the woods with no hearth and no name. The Oss will bring them in. Fill the fold with ten of them and the people will know we can feed the fires for a long winter.

041.text: This neighbour is not idle. Their warriors will come. Archers behind a line of spears will meet them, and the Cunning Woman can turn a blow aside.
041.shown: This neighbour is not idle. Their warriors will come. Archers behind a line of spears will meet them, and the Cunning Woman can turn a blow aside.

043.text: Two peoples have smelt our smoke, and both are coming for us. We cannot beat them and we have no camp to raise more warriors. But our valley is ringed with crags, and there are only three ways in. Plant blackthorn across the gaps, wake the bog beyond them, sink the ground under anyone who forces a way through, and hold the village for ten minutes until they tire of us. The altar gives twice what it usually does here; feed it.
043.shown: Two peoples have smelt our smoke, and both are coming for us. We cannot beat them and we have no camp to raise more warriors. But our valley is ringed with crags, and there are only three ways in. Plant blackthorn across the gaps, wake the bog beyond them, sink the ground under anyone who forces a way through, and hold the village for ten minutes until they tire of us. The altar gives twice what it usually does here; feed it.

045.text: Up here the land is broken into crags and there is barely room for two huts. Nobody can grow until they make level ground. Feed the altar, flatten the rock around the village, and build on what you make. Across the rocks one other people is just as cramped, and the first to spread out will win.
045.shown: Up here the land is broken into crags and there is barely room for two huts. Nobody can grow until they make level ground. Feed the altar, flatten the rock around the village, and build on what you make. Across the rocks one other people is just as cramped, and the first to spread out will win.

047.text: Every people here keeps its own island, and the sea is too deep and too wide for any bridge. Our enemies have learned to fly. Their balloonists drop fire on the huts and carry fighters over the water. Here a Cunning Woman does not come back: if ours dies we are finished, and if theirs dies so are they. Keep fighters sworn to her side, keep the Rook Trees watching, and when you are ready, put her in a balloon.
047.shown: Every people here keeps its own island, and the sea is too deep and too wide for any bridge. Our enemies have learned to fly. Their balloonists drop fire on the huts and carry fighters over the water. Here a Cunning Woman does not come back: if ours dies we are finished, and if theirs dies so are they. Keep fighters sworn to her side, keep the Rook Trees watching, and when you are ready, put her in a balloon.

049.text: Wicker is in short supply this season - if we are to survive, we shall need to do things in the oldest way. Crown the May Queen and exalt her for a season. Nature is a lustful mistress. Only the fairest of our daughters shall fit her for a bride. Crown her. Guard her. Attend her prime. Why then she shall dance her bloody nuptials and bring all favour upon us.
049.shown: Wicker is in short supply this season - if we are to survive, we shall need to do things in the oldest way. Crown the May Queen and exalt her for a season. Nature is a lustful mistress. Only the fairest of our daughters shall fit her for a bride. Crown her. Guard her. Attend her prime. Why then she shall dance her bloody nuptials and bring all favour upon us.

051.text: Twelve go into the belly of the ram and the whole world sees it burn. Fill it with strangers and the Cunning Woman will shake the earth beneath our enemies.
051.shown: Twelve go into the belly of the ram and the whole world sees it burn. Fill it with strangers and the Cunning Woman will shake the earth beneath our enemies.

053.text: Out in the wilds the old hills are hollow. Walk the Cunning Woman there with twenty of the faithful and fifteen hundred mana and she will never walk again; but she will see everything, and reach everywhere.
053.shown: Out in the wilds the old hills are hollow. Walk the Cunning Woman there with twenty of the faithful and fifteen hundred mana and she will never walk again; but she will see everything, and reach everywhere.

055.text: In the deep wood stands the dead oak. Hang the Cunning Woman from it for two minutes and the Hunt will ride for us, and every life they take will be ours. No wicker will burn in this wood, and our rivals know what the oak means: the moment she hangs, they will come for her. Guard the tree.
055.shown: In the deep wood stands the dead oak. Hang the Cunning Woman from it for two minutes and the Hunt will ride for us, and every life they take will be ours. No wicker will burn in this wood, and our rivals know what the oak means: the moment she hangs, they will come for her. Guard the tree.

057.text: Three peoples share these hills with us, and none of them will share for long. The mountains themselves can be made to burn.
057.shown: Three peoples share these hills with us, and none of them will share for long. The mountains themselves can be made to burn.

059.text: Four peoples on four islands, and no road, wing or spell will carry anyone across. There is only one way this ends. Grow, fill the wicker man, gather a full bar of mana, and call every soul to the stones at the heart of the world to settle it there.
059.shown: Four peoples on four islands, and no road, wing or spell will carry anyone across. There is only one way this ends. Grow, fill the wicker man, gather a full bar of mana, and call every soul to the stones at the heart of the world to settle it there.

061.text: The year turns cold and the rivals are hungry. Everything you have learned is yours to use.
061.shown: The year turns cold and the rivals are hungry. Everything you have learned is yours to use.

063.text: From here the land is not kind. Three peoples, each as cunning as we are. Nothing is held back from us, and nothing from them.
063.shown: From here the land is not kind. Three peoples, each as cunning as we are. Nothing is held back from us, and nothing from them.

065.text: We have settled in the middle of everything. Three narrow causeways run from the rival islands to ours, and every army will march along one of them. But we did not come empty-handed: our folds are full of the wild folk, and the Wicker God already stands in its grove, waiting to be fed.
065.shown: We have settled in the middle of everything. Three narrow causeways run from the rival islands to ours, and every army will march along one of them. But we did not come empty-handed: our folds are full of the wild folk, and the Wicker God already stands in its grove, waiting to be fed.

067.text: We arrive with little, and the others have been here for years. Their halls are built and their warriors drilled. We must be cleverer than them, because we cannot be stronger.
067.shown: We arrive with little, and the others have been here for years. Their halls are built and their warriors drilled. We must be cleverer than them, because we cannot be stronger.

069.text: Something has stirred the neighbours to fury. They will come early and often. Make them pay for every step.
069.shown: Something has stirred the neighbours to fury. They will come early and often. Make them pay for every step.

071.text: The sea has taken most of the world. What land is left is small and fought over, and the others are richer in offerings than we are.
071.shown: The sea has taken most of the world. What land is left is small and fought over, and the others are richer in offerings than we are.

073.text: This is the end of the year, and perhaps the end of us. Three strong peoples surround us and they have already begun. Only the bog, the thorn, the hollow hill and the Hunt can turn this. Rejoice, if we live.
073.shown: This is the end of the year, and perhaps the end of us. Three strong peoples surround us and they have already begun. Only the bog, the thorn, the hollow hill and the Hunt can turn this. Rejoice, if we live.

074.text: Scry where e're the beacon burns. For it shalbe thine eyes.
074.shown: Scry where e're the beacon burns. For it shalbe thine eyes.

075.text: Thy will readily done upon thine enemies.
075.shown: Thy will readily done upon thine enemies.

076.text: The strike of thunder is a blow no man or woman can survive.
076.shown: The strike of thunder is a blow no man or woman can survive.

077.text: Calls forth a cloud o’ wicked horseflies to bite and sting and scatter thy assailants for ten seconds.
077.shown: Calls forth a cloud o’ wicked horseflies to bite and sting and scatter thy assailants for ten seconds.

078.text: Turns wandering wildmen within the circle into your villagers.
078.shown: Turns wandering wildmen within the circle into your villagers.

079.text: A ward against harm for those within its ‘fluence.
079.shown: A ward against harm for those within its ‘fluence.

080.text: Raise the shades of dead men. Brief candles who make war, draw the eye and melt away come striking.
080.shown: Raise the shades of dead men. Brief candles who make war, draw the eye and melt away come striking.

081.text: Raise up a causeway towards heights and across water.
081.shown: Raise up a causeway towards heights and across water.

082.text: From crags and cliffsides spring forth green and level fields. Cannot be cast upon the water.
082.shown: From crags and cliffsides spring forth green and level fields. Cannot be cast upon the water.

083.text: Witch them to thy cause - they’ll fight for you for twenty-five seconds.
083.shown: Witch them to thy cause - they’ll fight for you for twenty-five seconds.

084.text: A twisting wind that tears walls from their foundations afore wand’ring in search of new victims.
084.shown: A twisting wind that tears walls from their foundations afore wand’ring in search of new victims.

085.text: A sucking mire that offers safe passage to those who know the way - and clammy death to those who do not. Will remain until ten are claimed.
085.shown: A sucking mire that offers safe passage to those who know the way - and clammy death to those who do not. Will remain until ten are claimed.

086.text: Creates a dyke within the downs to drown thy foes and their works.
086.shown: Creates a dyke within the downs to drown thy foes and their works.

087.text: Behold, the very earth shall shake and rupture.
087.shown: Behold, the very earth shall shake and rupture.

088.text: A bitter rain of stoney death. Watch as they flee their collapsing homes.
088.shown: A bitter rain of stoney death. Watch as they flee their collapsing homes.

089.text: Engender a plague of paroxysms, contagion and a bloody demise.
089.shown: Engender a plague of paroxysms, contagion and a bloody demise.

090.text: Nature’s cruellest vengeance at the command.
090.shown: Nature’s cruellest vengeance at the command.

091.text: There shalbe a moot at the world’s end and every living souls shalbe a soldier in the battle of all against all. So hath it been and so mote it be.
091.shown: There shalbe a moot at the world’s end and every living souls shalbe a soldier in the battle of all against all. So hath it been and so mote it be.

092.text: Trains osses, who roam and carry off captives
092.shown: Trains osses, who roam and carry off captives

093.text: A thorny barrier. Tap where it starts and where it ends; nothing walks through until it is hacked down
093.shown: A thorny barrier. Tap where it starts and where it ends; nothing walks through until it is hacked down

094.text: Villagers dance here, easing dread, until a May Queen is crowned
094.shown: Villagers dance here, easing dread, until a May Queen is crowned

095.text: A lookout high in a dead tree; sees far and hurls fire-pots at balloons
095.shown: A lookout high in a dead tree; sees far and hurls fire-pots at balloons

096.text: Pens up to fifteen captives your osses bring home
096.shown: Pens up to fifteen captives your osses bring home

097.text: Takes one offering at a time; stronger among trees
097.shown: Takes one offering at a time; stronger among trees

098.text: Holds twelve; burns for an enormous offering
098.shown: Holds twelve; burns for an enormous offering

099.text: A burning beacon; the land around it stays in sight while it stands
099.shown: A burning beacon; the land around it stays in sight while it stands

100.text: Your Cunning Woman lies sealed here
100.shown: Your Cunning Woman lies sealed here

101.text: Hang your Cunning Woman from it for two minutes and the Wild Hunt rides
101.shown: Hang your Cunning Woman from it for two minutes and the Wild Hunt rides

102.text: Holds five; burns for mana and a frenzy
102.shown: Holds five; burns for mana and a frenzy

103.text: Your Cunning Woman is reborn here
103.shown: Your Cunning Woman is reborn here

104.text: Seal your Cunning Woman inside with twenty followers and 1,500 mana
104.shown: Seal your Cunning Woman inside with twenty followers and 1,500 mana

105.text: Where every people gathers at the end
105.shown: Where every people gathers at the end

106.text: Your bog has drowned {TUNE.swampLives} and drains away, sated.
106.shown: Your bog has drowned {number} and drains away, sated.

107.text: Your Cunning Woman has fallen. She returns to the stone circle in {TUNE.shamanRespawn} seconds.
107.shown: Your Cunning Woman has fallen. She returns to the stone circle in {number} seconds.

109.text: This ground has been salted. Nothing of yours will stand here for a while
109.shown: This ground has been salted. Nothing of yours will stand here for a while

110.text: Herne's Oak must stand in deep woodland
110.shown: Herne's Oak must stand in deep woodland

111.text: A forest altar must stand among trees
111.shown: A forest altar must stand among trees

112.text: There is no ground for it at the edge of the village
112.shown: There is no ground for it at the edge of the village

113.text: Your Cunning Woman walks to the edge of the village. Your people gather below to watch.
113.shown: Your Cunning Woman walks to the edge of the village. Your people gather below to watch.

114.text: She is gone over the edge. {LEAP_N} of your people step out from among the stones, and for a while even your enemies are still.
114.shown: She is gone over the edge. {number} of your people step out from among the stones, and for a while even your enemies are still.

115.text: Your tomb has fallen, and your Cunning Woman with it. Here she does not come back.
